headline: Medium risk: shared-output and workflow assumptions create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways, but no direct shared runtime is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can consume artifacts and API-driven inputs, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt-content repository that could be copied into workflows. No shared channel is documented, so the injection path is indirect and likely manual rather than automatic.
conditions: IF operator copies prompt text from agent_b into agent_a workflow parameters or artifacts
IF agent_a treats artifact contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict copied prompt text to a review-only staging step
Add a manual provenance check before any prompt is reused
Use a fixed allowlist of workflow parameters
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or templating separation in the workflow layer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress; agent B has no documented data classes or write surfaces. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not evidenced beyond a small, indirect workflow risk.
conditions: IF sensitive artifacts are placed into agent_a inputs and then copied into agent_b-managed content
IF agent_a egress is configured to send those artifacts to external services
mitigations: Keep sensitive artifacts out of shared prompts
Review allowlisted egress destinations before execution
Separate storage for workflow inputs and editorial content
requires-engineering: enforce per-class data handling and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows exposes REST/GRPC and allowlisted egress, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering has no documented write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable state, a capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is extended with write access to the same mutable resource as agent_a
IF both agents are granted the same OAuth or filesystem write scope
mitigations: Do not grant shared write scopes
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable backend is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can produce workflow artifacts and parameters that agent B could reuse as content or guidance, and B is a prompt-engineering content source with no documented verification step. The pair therefore supports an A-to-B trust chain in default documentation, though not a direct action-taking chain.
conditions: IF agent_b reuses agent_a outputs as authoritative guidance without verification
IF workflow artifacts from agent_a are published into agent_b-facing content
mitigations: Require a human verification step before reuse
Label agent_a outputs as untrusted drafts
Add source citations to any reused workflow artifact
requires-engineering: implement provenance tracking between workflow outputs and content publication

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Agent A is open-source workflow software and agent B is an open-source prompt repository, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway to compare.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed under a regulated data policy not shown in the profiles
IF sensitive regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow
mitigations: Document data residency for any deployment
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement to the orchestrator
